text:
jordan: Quick sync — thinking through calibration pool splitting for the next quant bakeoff (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ). Want a reproducible, production-representative sample that also catches edge cases. Opinions?

mia: +1 on reproducible. My proposal: stratify by task class (summarization, code, Q/A, instruction-following), by token-length bucket, and by failure-mode tags (hallucination, truncation). Then apply weighted sampling to match production token distribution.

sam: That sounds good. Also add a small adversarial shard (~5-10%) with perturbations and corner-case prompts — we need to see worst-case accuracy deltas after quant.

jordan: How big should the pool be? Our previous quick runs used ~2k prompts but noise was high for per-task metrics.

mia: For stable per-task deltas I recommend ~5k–10k total. Stratified: 3k baseline (prod-weighted), 1k edge/adversarial, 1k diversity holdout (for cross-val). Keep seeds fixed.

sam: Agree with holdout. Also dedupe aggressively across canonicalization (whitespace, punctuation). We saw duplicates artificially deflate delta in past runs.

eva: On dedupe: use normalized hashing + semantic dedupe for paraphrases if possible. But don't over-clean — we want near-duplicates that happen in prod. Suggest dedupe_threshold=0.9 for semantic sims.

jordan: Good point. Mia, can you sketch the sampling CLI we can run in the eval infra?

mia: Sure — rough prototype:
```
python tools/sample_calib.py \
  --input datasets/combined_catalog.jsonl \
  --strata task_class,length_bucket,failure_tag \
  --weights prod_token_weights.json \
  --adv-share 0.08 \
  --holdout 0.1 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output calib/pool-2026-01.jsonl
```
This will output meta fields: task_class, length_bucket, orig_source, normalized_text, hash.

sam: Nice. For adversarial generation we can auto-mutate 20% of the edge set: insert long numeric sequences, non-UTF chars, nested code fences. Those trigger quantized-kernel path differences.

eva: For metrics, track per-example DeltaLL, token-error-rate, and embedding-cosine-drift. Report median and 90th-percentile deltas per strata. Avoid only mean — heavy tails matter.

jordan: Also add a binary "regression" flag if DeltaLL > threshold or logits-change causes argmax switch for classification tasks. That helps build pass/fail criteria for model variants.

mia: Implementation note: avoid leaking eval labels into the sample selection. The sampling should be blind to model outputs. Only use metadata and production signals.

sam: On quant method comparisons — AWQ seems to affect token-level logits more for long sequences vs GPTQ which perturbs embeddings more. So ensure long-token bucket gets extra weight for AWQ runs.

eva: We should version the pool and store a manifest with commit hash + sampling seed + strata config. This makes reruns exact and audit-friendly.

jordan: CI integration idea: on PR that registers a new quantized build, run a cheap quick-check subset (200 examples) then queue full bakeoff async. CI quick-check should run same seed but smaller.

ci-bot: quick-check triggered by PR #1429 — sample subset 200 seeded 42, estimated runtime 18m, will post results in thread when done.

mia: One last ops caveat — when matching prod token distribution, use rolling window of last 30 days to avoid historic skews. Keep a stable snapshot for comparability across bakeoffs.

sam: Agreed. I'll draft the adversarial mutation recipes and contribute to tools/sample_calib.py.

eva: I'll write the metrics schema (DeltaLL thresholds, embedding drift cutoffs) and a doc for interpretation.

jordan: Great — thanks team. Action items: mia = implement sampling CLI & manifest; sam = adversarial mutations; eva = metrics schema; me = wire into bakeoff runner. Follow up in #eng-ml next week. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: calib-checker completed for sample subset: dup_rate=3.9%, avg_len=78, adv_share=0.08, seed=42. No immediate regressions in quick-check.
